title: Upgrade The Content Admin To 0.14.0
userRequest: Update @codeyam/cms to the latest version (0.13.0 -> 0.14.0) and make sure content is migrated appropriately, first checking whether there are changes Nicole made that need to be saved.
description:
Moved @codeyam/cms from 0.13.0 to 0.14.0, whose feature is a live page preview inside the entry editor: the entry's real page renders in an iframe beside the form and follows what the editor types, replacing the save-then-open-a-tab loop. Three states are covered by existing scenarios rather than new ones — an entry with a page (cms-chapter-editor-new-york-city), a collection declared with no page (cms-analytics-and-embeds, which is siteIntegrations and the only null path), and a blank creation form (cms-entry-editor-new-chapter-form). NO CONTENT MIGRATION WAS REQUIRED, and that is a finding rather than an assumption: a file-by-file diff of pristine 0.13.0 against pristine 0.14.0 shows changes confined to the admin's own src/, with no collection, field, schema, template or dependency change, and the commit touches nothing under src/content or src/data. This is also the first of five CMS upgrades where the reorder-arrows patch needed NO re-derivation — 0.14.0 changed only entry-EDITOR files while the patch edits the entry LIST, so a renamed patch applied with zero fuzz. The arrows were then verified present on a served /admin page (eight move controls), not merely inferred from a 200, because CMS_SETUP.md records that every prior failure here compiled, passed every check, and silently dropped the arrows.

The upgrade also changed what the SITE's pages do, which was not in the plan and is the reason this cycle carries a src/ change at all. Embedding the real page in the editor means every third-party tag in that page's head now fires once per entry an editor opens: Google Analytics (G-GCBX577FFD, live) was recording the team's own editing as site traffic — permanently wrong data, since those page_views cannot be separated afterwards — and Givebutter was loading a live donation form inside an editing tool. src/lib/embeddedPreview.ts reads the CMS's own cms-embed flag and both Analytics.astro and GivebutterWidgets.astro now inject their tag through loadScriptUnlessEmbedded instead of emitting <script is:inline src>, which is what lets a statically built page make a decision only the browser can make. Verified in both directions: a reader on /donate and /chapters/nyc still gets all five third-party requests, the editor pane gets zero. Eleven tests cover it, and CMS_SETUP.md now carries the re-check for the next upgrade.

Two repairs were made that this upgrade surfaced but did not cause. The MomentumAccomplishments isolation route was reading donatePage.accomplishments, a key that no longer exists since those entries moved into the CMS-editable accomplishments collection; `?? []` turned the miss into an empty array, the band hides itself when empty, and the scenario had been capturing a BLANK page while every gate reported green. It now calls loadAccomplishments(), the same loader /donate uses, so the two cannot drift again. Separately, the editor's preview proxy wedged mid-session and captures taken against the half-dead server baked Astro crash pages into three unrelated frames (BoardMemberTile, a chapter gallery, the cutover runbook); those were restored from HEAD and every one of the 88 changed screenshots was screened by mean luminance plus eye before being kept.

SCOPE VERDICT: this cycle delivers none of the project's five deliverables and closes none of them. It is maintenance on the content admin, so 'a content admin that runs locally', 'the content admin in the cloud on GitHub Pages' and 'the content admin protected by a password and/or GitHub sign-in' remain open and are improved but not completed; 'faithfully reproduce the site' and 'publish it live on GitHub Pages' are untouched, the latter belonging to the assist track rather than a build cycle. All five are deferred by explicit user decision — the user scoped this session to the CMS update alone.

DEFERRED BY USER DECISION, not oversight: seven CMS-authored commits by Nicole sit unmerged on origin/staging (three complete volunteer roles, a photo on the events role, and her real Jessica Li testimonial typed into momentumSections/testimonials.md — the band-POSITION descriptor, which renders nothing — while testimonials/jessica-li.md on main still holds invented placeholder copy). The user chose to rescue that content in a separate session, to replace the placeholder with her real words, and NOT to merge staging into main. Nothing is lost; it stays on staging.
